text: From the study by Bandura et al. (aggression):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Scenes from the International Affective Picture System stimuli set were used. Each scene
had been rated in two ways.
Name these two ways.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe one methodological weakness of this study.

text: From the study by Canli et al. (brain scans and emotions):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the sample used in Experiment 1 of this study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one result from the ‘Memory or Belief?’ questionnaire from Experiment 1 of this
study.

text: From the study by Laney et al. (false memory):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the experimenter feedback given to a participant if they did not want to continue
with this study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Studies in social psychology can be used to help teachers in the classroom.
Suggest how this study could be used to help a teacher with a disobedient class. Your
suggestion must be ethical.

text: From the study by Milgram (obedience):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline one aim of this study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one reason why the procedure was standardised in this study.

text: From the study by Baron-Cohen et al. (eyes test):
The debate about individual and situational explanations relates to the study by Pepperberg
(parrot learning).
Outline what is meant by this debate. Include one example from the individual explanation and
one example from the situational explanation from the study by Pepperberg.
From the study by Yamamoto et al. (chimpanzee helping):
Describe the procedure for the ‘Cannot See’ condition.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline how monitoring performance was scored.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Two friends, Seth and Jamie, are discussing this study in terms of generalisability.
Seth believes the study does have generalisability but Jamie believes the study does not
have generalisability.
Outline why you think either Seth or Jamie is correct, using evidence from the study.

text: From the study by Andrade (doodling):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the psychology being investigated in the study by Saavedra and Silverman (button
phobia).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain whether each ethical guideline below was broken in the study by Saavedra and
Silverman (button phobia):
confidentiality ______
informed consent ______
privacy ______
protection from psychological harm ______

two weaknesses. At least one of your evaluation points must be about qualitative data.
